topics.title: Definition and Scope of Government
objectives: i. define Government as an institution
ii. state the characteristics of Government
iii. explain the functions of Government

topics.title: Basic Concepts of Government
items: a. Power, Influence, Authority, Legitimacy, Sovereignty
b. Society, State, Nation, Nation-State
c. Political Processes; Political Socialization, Political Participation, Political Culture
objectives: i. identify the fundamental concepts in governance
ii. analyse various political processes
iii. explain the relationship of the state to Government

topics.title: Forms of Government
items: Monarchy, Aristocracy, Oligarchy, Autocracy, Republicanism, Democracy-definitions, features, merits and demerits
objectives: i. distinguish between different forms of government
ii. discuss the features of each of the forms of Government

topics.title: Arms of Government
items: a. The Legislature – types, structure, functions, powers
b. The Executive – types, functions, powers
c. The Judiciary – functions, powers, components
d. Their relationships
objectives: i. identify the duties and obligations of the various arms of government and their agencies
ii. relate each arm to its functions
iii. appreciate how these arms interrelates

topics.title: Structures of Governance
items: a. Unitary – features, reasons for adoption, merits and demerits
b. Federal – features, reasons for adoption, merits and demerits
c. Confederal - features, reasons for adoption, merits and demerits
objectives: i. compare the various political structures of governance
ii. understand the reasons for the adoption of any of these structures of governance

topics.title: Systems of Governance
items: Presidential, Parliamentary and Monarchical, features, merits and demerits
objectives: i. distinguish between the different systems of governance
ii. analyse the features, merits and demerits of each system of governance

topics.title: Political Ideologies
items: Communalism, Feudalism, Capitalism, Socialism, Communism, Totalitarianism, Fascism, Nazism, Liberalism
objectives: i. differentiate between the major political ideologies
ii. contrast their modes of production

topics.title: Constitution
items: Meaning, Sources, Functions, Types - Written, Unwritten, Rigid and Flexible
objectives: i. Define and identify sources and functions of constitutions
ii. compare the nature of constitutions

topics.title: Principles of Democratic Government
items: Ethics and Accountability in Public Office, Separation of Power, Checks and Balances, Individual and Collective Responsibility, Constitutionalism, Rule of Law, Representative Government, Centralization and Decentralization of Government
objectives: i. identify the principles of democratic government
ii. determine the application of these principles

topics.title: Processes of Legislation
items: Legislative Enactments – Acts, Edicts, Bye-laws, Delegated Legislation, Decrees
objectives: i. analyse the processes involved in the making of laws

topics.title: Citizenship
items: a. Meaning, types
b. Citizenship rights
c. Dual citizenship, renunciation, deprivation
d. Duties and obligations of citizens
e. Duties and obligations of the state
objectives: i. differentiate between the various methods of acquiring citizenship
ii. specify the rights and responsibilities of a citizen
iii. assess the obligations of the state

topics.title: The Electoral Process
items: a. Suffrage – evolution, types
b. Election – types, ingredients of free and fair election, pre-and post-election crisis
c. Electoral System - types, advantages and disadvantages of each
d. Electoral Commission – functions, problems
objectives: i. distinguish the different types of franchise
ii. identify and explain the types of electoral systems
iii. analyse the various electoral processes

topics.title: Political Parties and Party Systems
items: a. Political parties – Definition, organization, functions
b. Party Systems – Definition, organization, functions, merits and demerits
objectives: i. assess the role of political parties
ii. distinguish between types of party systems

topics.title: Pressure Groups
items: a. Definition, types, functions and modes of operation
b. Differences between Pressure Groups and Political Parties
objectives: i. evaluate the functions and the modus operandi of pressure groups
ii. distinguish between pressure groups and political parties

topics.title: Public Opinion
items: a. Meaning, formation and measurement
b. Functions and limitations
objectives: i. compare methods of assessing public opinion
ii. assess the functions of public opinion
iii. analyse the limitations of public opinion

topics.title: The Civil Service/Public Service
items: a. Definition, characteristics, functions, structure, control and problems of the civil service
b. Definition, characteristics, functions, structure, control and problems of the public service
objectives: i. analyse the significance of civil service in governance
ii. distinguish between the civil service and public service

topics.title: Pre – colonial Polities
items: Pre-jihad Hausa/Fulani Emirate, Tiv, Igbo, Yoruba
a. Their structural organization
b. The functions of their various political institutions
objectives: i. appreciate the effectiveness of the pre-colonial political systems
ii. compare pre-colonial systems of governance

topics.title: Imperialists Penetration
items: a. The British process of acquisition – trade, missionary activities, company rule, crown colony, protectorate
b. The British colonial administrative policy – direct and indirect rule
c. The French colonial administrative policy – assimilation and association
d. Impact of British colonial rule-economic, political, socio-cultural
e. Comparison of British and French colonial administration
objectives: i. trace the processes of imperialists penetration
ii. assess the impact of British and French colonial policies
iii. distinguish between British and French colonial practices

topics.title: Process of Decolonization
items: a. Nationalism – Meaning, Types
b. Nationalist Movements – emergence, goals, strategies
c. Nationalist Leaders – Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello, Ladipo Solanke, Aminu Kano, J. S. Tarka, Tafawa Balewa and others
d. Emergence of Nationalist Parties
e. Influence of external factors
objectives: i. evaluate the process of decolonization
ii. assess the roles of nationalist leaders and parties
iii. assess the impact of external forces and ideas (Pan-Africanism, Back–to–Africa Movements, Second World War etc.)

topics.title: Constitutional Development in Nigeria
items: a. Hugh Clifford Constitution (1922)
b. Arthur Richards Constitution (1946)
c. John Macpherson Constitution (1951)
d. Oliver Lyttleton Constitution (1954)
e. Independence Constitution (1960) Their features, merits and demerits
objectives: i. compare the various constitutional developments
ii. analyse the merits and demerits of each of the constitutions

topics.title: Post – Independence Constitutions
items: 1963, 1979, 1989 and 1999 (As Amended) characteristics and shortcomings
objectives: i. assess the workings of the various Constitutions
ii. analyse the merits and demerits of the Post-Independence Constitutions in Nigeria

topics.title: Institutions of Government in the Post – Independence Nigeria
items: a. The Legislative – structures, functions and workings
b. The Executive – structure, functions and workings
c. The Judiciary – structure, functions and workings
objectives: i. evaluate the operations of the Arms of government and their agencies, e.g., the Civil Service, Armed Forces, Police, Courts and others

topics.title: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
items: The Civil Service Commission, the Public Complaints Commission, Electoral Commissions, National Boundary Commission, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and Others – objectives functions and problems
objectives: i. evaluate the operations of Public Commissions
ii. assess the problems of the Public Commissions and their constraints

topics.title: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria
items: a. First Republic
b. Second Republic
c. Third Republic
d. Fourth Republic - Evolution, membership spread, structure, etc
objectives: i. contrast political processes in the republics
ii. evaluate the ideologies, structure and composition of the political parties

topics.title: The Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism
items: a. Rationale for a Federal System
b. Tiers of Government and their relationship
d. Problems of Nigerian Federalism – Census, Revenue Allocation, Conflicts etc. solutions e.g. The Federal Character Principle, etc
objectives: i. examine the workings of Nigerian federalism
ii. identify its problems
iii. evaluate the corrective measures to be adopted

topics.title: Public Corporations and Parastatals
items: a. Definition, types, purpose and functions
b. Finance, control and problems
c. Deregulation, Privatization and Commercialization – objectives, features, merits and demerits
d. Comparison between Public Corporations and parastatals
objectives: i. examine the operations of public corporations and parastatals
ii. identify the processes involved in privatization and commercialization
iii. assess the economic importance of privatization and commercialization

topics.title: Local Government
items: a. Local Government Administration prior to 1976
b. Features of Local Government Reforms (1976, 1989) – structure, functions, finance and inter-governmental relations
c. Traditional Rulers and Local Governments
d. Problems of Local Government Administration in Nigeria
objectives: i. trace the evolution and structure of Local Government
ii. identify the major problems faced by Local Governments
iii. analyse the roles of Traditional Rulers in the Local Government system in Nigeria

topics.title: The Military in Nigerian Politics
items: a. Factors that led to military intervention
b. Structure of military regimes
c. Impact of military rule – political, e.g. creation of states, NYSC, introduction of unitary system (Unification Decree NO. 34) etc. economic, e.g. SAP, DFRRI, Peoples Bank, MAMSER, etc
d. Processes of military disengagement
objectives: i. evaluate the reasons given for military intervention
ii. assess the achievements of military rule
iii. determine the conditions that necessitated withdrawal from the political scene

sections.title: FOREIGN POLICY AND NIGERIA’S RELATIONSHIP WITH THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY

topics.title: Foreign Policy
items: Definition, purpose, determining factors; formulation and implementation
objectives: i. Define foreign policy, identify and explain its determinants

topics.title: Nigeria’s Foreign Policy
items: a. Relations with major powers
b. Relations with developing countries, e.g. the Technical Aid Corps (TAC), Peace-Keeping Operations etc
c. Nigeria’s Non-Alignment Policy
objectives: i. identify the major objectives of Nigeria’s foreign policy
ii. analyse Nigeria’s non-aligned posture during the cold war

topics.title: Nigeria’s Relations with African Countries
items: a. Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy – guiding principles, implementation and implications
b. NEPAD – origin, objectives and implications
objectives: i. evaluate the role of Nigeria in continental affairs
ii. assess the role of NEPAD in developing Africa

topics.title: Nigeria in International Organizations
items: a. The United Nations
b. The Commonwealth
c. The Organization of African Unity
d. The African Union
e. The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
f. The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
objectives: i. analyse the dynamics of Nigeria’s involvement in international organizations
ii. assess their contribution to the development of Nigeria

topics.title: International Organizations
items: a. ECOWAS
b. OAU, AU
c. Commonwealth
d. OPEC
e. UNO
f. African Petroleum Producers Association; - Origin, objectives, structure, functions, achievements, problems and prospects of these organizations
objectives: i. evaluate the operations of these international organizations
ii. assess the role of these organizations in world affairs
iii. appreciate the challenges of these organizations and how they can be overcome
